content: 1. The effectiveness of delafloxacin can be reduced due to cation binding in the gastrointestinal (GI) tract. This occurs because oral delafloxacin forms chelates with alkaline earth and transition metal cations. To minimize this interaction, administer oral delafloxacin at least 2 hours before or 6 hours after agents containing these cations. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored. 2. Delafloxacin may decrease the efficacy of oral microbiota products due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. Oral microbiota products contain bacterial spores, and co-administration with antibacterial agents may reduce their effectiveness. Complete the antibiotic regimen 2-4 days before initiating oral microbiota therapy. Monitor the patient closely or consider alternative treatments. 3. Multivitamins can reduce the levels or effects of delafloxacin by cation binding in the GI tract. Oral delafloxacin forms chelates with alkaline earth and transition metal cations. Administer oral delafloxacin at least 2 hours before or 6 hours after taking multivitamins. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored. 4. Polysaccharide iron can decrease the levels or effects of delafloxacin by cation binding in the GI tract. Oral delafloxacin forms chelates with alkaline earth and transition metal cations. Administer oral delafloxacin at least 2 hours before or 6 hours after taking polysaccharide iron. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored. 5. Selinexor and delafloxacin may interact through an unspecified mechanism. Patients treated with selinexor may experience neurological toxicities. Avoid combining selinexor with other medications that can cause dizziness or confusion. Use alternative drugs or monitor closely. 6. Magnesium sulfate and potassium chloride can reduce delafloxacin levels by inhibiting its GI absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Administer fluoroquinolones at least 2 hours before and no less than 6 hours after each dose to avoid chelation with magnesium. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored. 7. Sodium sulfate, potassium sulfate, and magnesium sulfate can reduce delafloxacin levels by inhibiting its GI absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Administer fluoroquinolones at least 2 hours before and no less than 6 hours after each dose to avoid chelation with magnesium. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored. 8. Sucralfate can decrease the levels or effects of delafloxacin by cation binding in the GI tract. Oral delafloxacin forms chelates with alkaline earth and transition metal cations. Administer oral delafloxacin at least 2 hours before or 6 hours after taking sucralfate. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored. 9. Delafloxacin may increase the effects of warfarin through an unspecified interaction mechanism. Use caution and monitor the patient closely. 10. Zinc can reduce the levels or effects of delafloxacin by cation binding in the GI tract. Oral delafloxacin forms chelates with alkaline earth and transition metal cations. Administer oral delafloxacin at least 2 hours before or 6 hours after taking zinc. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored. 11. Common adverse effects of delafloxacin include nausea (8%), diarrhea (8%), headache (3%), transaminase elevations (3%), and vomiting (2%). Fluoroquinolones, including delafloxacin, have been associated with disabling and potentially irreversible serious adverse reactions, such as tendinitis, tendon rupture, peripheral neuropathy, and central nervous system (CNS) effects. Discontinue the drug immediately if any of these serious adverse reactions occur, and avoid systemic fluoroquinolones in patients who experience these effects. 12. Fluoroquinolones may exacerbate muscle weakness in patients with myasthenia gravis. Avoid their use in patients with a known history of myasthenia gravis. 13. Delafloxacin is contraindicated in patients with hypersensitivity to delafloxacin, its components, or other fluoroquinolones. 14. Prescribing antibiotics in the absence of a proven or strongly suspected bacterial infection is unlikely to provide benefit and increases the risk of developing drug-resistant bacteria. 15. Epidemiologic studies have observed an increased risk of aortic aneurysm and dissection within 2 months following fluoroquinolone use, particularly in elderly patients. The etiology of this risk is not identified. Reserve fluoroquinolones for patients with known or greater risk for aortic aneurysm only when no alternative antibacterial treatments are available. 16. Blood glucose disturbances, including symptomatic hyperglycemia and hypoglycemia, have been reported with fluoroquinolones, usually in diabetic patients receiving concomitant treatment with oral hypoglycemic agents (e.g., glyburide) or insulin. Careful blood glucose monitoring is recommended. Severe cases of hypoglycemia resulting in coma or death have been reported with other fluoroquinolones. If a hypoglycemic reaction occurs, discontinue therapy and initiate appropriate treatment immediately. 17. Data on the use of delafloxacin in pregnant women are limited and insufficient to inform a drug-associated risk of major birth defects or miscarriages. It is unknown if delafloxacin is distributed in human breast milk, but it is excreted in the breast milk of rats. Consider the developmental and health benefits of breastfeeding along with the mother’s clinical need for the drug and any potential adverse effects on the breastfed infant from the drug or the underlying maternal condition. 18. Delafloxacin is generally acceptable for use during pregnancy. Controlled studies in pregnant women show no evidence of fetal risk. 19. For intravenous (IV) administration, infuse delafloxacin over 60 minutes using a volume control set or piggyback container. The drug may be taken with or without food. If a dose is missed, take it as soon as possible within 4 hours of the missed dose. If more than 4 hours have passed, wait until the next scheduled dose. 20. Store delafloxacin tablets and lyophilized powder at controlled room temperature (20-25°C or 68-77°F), with excursions permitted to 15-30°C (59-86°F). Reconstituted vials can be refrigerated (2-8°C or 36-46°F) for up to 24 hours or kept at controlled room temperature until further diluted for IV infusion. Do not freeze. Diluted solutions can also be refrigerated or kept at controlled room temperature for up to 24 hours. Do not freeze. 21.
